questions.q: According to Hyman, what sits at the root of today's health, inequality and environmental crises?
a: The rapid rise of social media
The growing cost of medical care
questions.why: The first lesson traces the world's biggest problems, from disease to poverty, back to the food we eat.

questions.q: What does the summary say happens to carbon when soil is over-farmed?
a: More CO2 is released than by all fossil fuel companies combined
Soil absorbs more CO2 than the world's forests do
CO2 output stays roughly the same as before
CO2 is turned into nitrogen fertilizer
questions.why: The second lesson calls soil the biggest CO2 absorber and warns that over-farming releases more than fossil fuel firms do.

questions.q: How many harvests does the summary say may be left if farming keeps degrading soil?
questions.why: The second lesson cites an estimate that only around 60 harvests remain at current rates of soil damage.

questions.q: Which farming practice does the summary recommend to stop destroying soil?
a: Growing one crop on large fields
questions.why: The third lesson lists no-till methods, crop rotation and mixed planting as parts of regenerative agriculture.

questions.q: Which seafood does the summary suggest choosing?
questions.why: The third lesson advises wild-caught salmon and anchovies over tuna and halibut, and less meat overall.
